articles.title: Not a Night Owl? The Arietid Meteor Shower Peaks at Dawn—and You Can Hear It on FM Radio
articles.summary: The Arietid meteor shower peaks around June 10, but you'll need to look east just before sunrise. Even cooler: tune an FM radio to static and listen for bursts of sound caused by meteor trails.

articles.title: From Seafloor to Summit: How a Desert Ridge in the UAE Unlocks 200,000 Years of Human History
articles.summary: Jabal al Fāyah, a limestone ridge in Sharjah, was once a seabed. Today, its fossils and stone tools reveal early human occupation dating back 210,000 years, making it a key site for understanding migration out of Africa.

articles.title: When Senses Collide: The Science of Synesthesia and Why Some People See Music
articles.summary: Synesthesia is a neurological trait where senses blend—like tasting colors or seeing sounds. Affecting up to 4% of people, it's linked to genes and has inspired artists from Van Gogh to Billie Eilish.
